title: 2011 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 11
statement: Let \(H\) be the intersection of the three altitudes of triangle \(A B C\). (This point is usually called the orthocenter). Prove that \(\angle D A H=\angle M A O\).

solutions.text: Note that since both \(A H\) and \(O X\) are perpendicular to \(B C\), it follows that \(A H \| O X\), so \(\angle D A H=\angle D X O=\angle A X O=\angle M A O\), as desired.
